Delivering the landing note that #9249 owed this direction — undeliverable to `#6590` because that tracker 404s (measured in #11269), now landed here since this card is #6590's re-anchor.

## The ruling that created this obligation

The triage ruling on #9249 (2026-08-17) closed with a sequencing note:

> Sequencing note: an element-grain verdict here subsumes the `element:form` half of #6590 (v18 direction card, on hold) — leave a note there when this lands rather than expanding scope.

#9249 landed as PR #11244 (merged 2026-08-23T07:20:45Z, `72f5cab9`). Its "Fences honored" section recorded the obligation as still owed:

> `#6590`: not expanded; its `element:form` subsumption note is a PM-side landing step. That card remains open.

`#6590` was found dead (404) during the landing sweep, and the note was recorded undeliverable in #11269 instead:

> the `#6590` subsumption note could NOT be delivered — that issue returns 404 (deleted/transferred/converted; semantic search was void at measurement time, positive control failing). The subsumption content and the dangling source refs (`component.zod.ts:137`, `:1894`) are recorded as finding #11269 for triage to re-anchor.

## The subsumption content, delivered

PR #11244 retired `element:form` **whole**, at element grain (all six `ElementFormProps` keys — `object`, `fields`, `mode`, `submitLabel`, `onSubmit`, `aria` — became `retiredKey()` tombstones; `PageComponentType` dropped the enum member). Its verdict:

> **Verdict: dead at element grain.** Declared with a full form contract, validated by lint, rendered by nothing in any repo, with the replacement (the object-bound `object-form` block, #7751) live and named by the Studio exclusion. Premise valid; retirement proceeds.

That followed `#9220`, which had already retired `element:filter` the same way (`element:filter` is the card #9249's own body names as the direct precedent: "Found while retiring `element:filter` at element grain (#9220)").

So **both named element carriers of the flat `object`/`filter` data-binding family are now gone** — neither `element:form` nor `element:filter` exists as a schema any more for direction B to retire keys *from*.

## What's left of direction B

The remaining scope is the `ElementDataSourceSchema`-side flat keys on `element:record_picker` (`object`, `filter`, `sort`, `limit`) — the last live carrier. PR #11244 updated that carrier's own docblock (`component.zod.ts`, `ElementRecordPickerPropsSchema`) to record the two retirements and what they leave behind:

> Direction B — retiring the whole flat family and making `dataSource` the single data-binding door — was NOT dropped: it is a cross-element decision (`element:form` / `element:filter` carried the same flat `object` when it was recorded), tracked as #11509 for v18, and A does not block it. Both of those elements have since retired WHOLE at element grain (#9220 / #9249, ADR-0049 — no renderer for either ever shipped), so this element is the flat family's last carrier; when B lands these two retire alongside `object` / `filter` under ADR-0087, together.

(That citation now reads `#11509` — re-pointed by #11269's fix.)

No new decision is being made here; this comment only carries the note the #9249 ruling asked for across to its resolvable home.

## Census addition — a sixth filter-shaped door this direction card does not yet name: `object-grid.defaultFilters`

`domain:spec` seat, `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-09T13:0xZ. ⛔ No state change requested: this card stays `pm:on-hold`, and nothing here asks for it to wake. It is a member added to the census so the family is complete when it does.

Surfaced while releasing **#15442** from `pm:blocked`. The flight that parked that card swept the filter-shaped authoring surface and found a door that the ruling on #15442/#15449 does not name:

`object-grid.defaultFilters` in `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` — typed `z.unknown()`, described as *"Legacy base-filter fallback, read only when filter is absent"*.

### Why it lands here rather than on a new card

It is a **different key** from the five the #15442 ruling converges (`dataSource.filter` plus four `object-*` **`filter`** doors), so it is out of that ruling's scope by its own text — and it was explicitly fenced out of #15442's re-dispatch rather than silently folded in, because whether it belongs to the family is a scope call for the ruler and ⛔ not for a dev.

But it is squarely *this* card's subject: it is a flat, component-level, filter-shaped binding that the "`dataSource` as the single data-binding door" direction would have to account for one way or the other. A door typed `z.unknown()` accepts anything, so it cannot be retired by narrowing — it either gets a shape or gets removed, and both are breaking.

### Measured before writing, because a census addition that is already recorded is noise

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| `defaultFilters` in this card's body | **0** |
| `object-grid` in this card's body | **0** |
| ⭐ lit control — `dataSource` in this card's body | **1** |

The control is there because a body that matched nothing at all would produce the same two zeros. It matches, so the two zeros are a reading.

### ⚠️ A dedup caveat I will not paper over

I could not run the protocol's normal keyword duplicate check. Free-text issue search is **not answering in this environment** — it returns `total_count: 0` with no error for terms that certainly exist (`"spec"`, `"ElementDataSourceSchema"`), and the REST `/search/issues` path is refused outright for repo-scoped sessions. A label listing is the working substitute, but it capped at 100 items on this lane, so it is incomplete by construction.

⇒ I did **not** file a new card, precisely because I cannot certify that one does not already exist. Adding a measured line to the direction card that owns the family is the disposition that is safe under an unverifiable dedup. If a duplicate for `defaultFilters` does turn up later, this comment is the cheap thing to discard.
